_comment: Known differences (AB-520): where the Java implementation may differ from the COBOL golden output. Only for quirks whose decision in the quirk register is 'fix', each linked to that decision. sign_off is 'pending' until the quirk owner approves; PARITY_REQUIRE_SIGNOFF=1 (go-live gate, ADR 0001) rejects pending entries. paths: '*' (whole case) or result paths such as effects[*].text.DECISION_REASON.

differences.reason: 29 Feb expiry: Java computes a valid next-year expiry (recommended 28 Feb) instead of the invalid 20250229 that DB2 rejects; the partial update path (Q-07) disappears with it.
Zero-premium renewal: COBOL abends on the rate-change division; Java guards the division.
Java clamps negative scores and carries the full score in the message and display instead of the 3-digit truncation.
Java does not truncate the loss ratio, so a loss ratio of 1000% or more gets the +200 surcharge.
Java keeps the accumulation reason; score and decision code must still match.
